sections.h2: Three ways to sell a Lancaster house
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, find a buyer yourself, or sell for cash. The right pick depends on how soon you need to be finished and the condition of the building. A tidy ranch with no deadline suits a listing. A failing roof, a probate to settle or a tenant who will not leave points toward a quick as-is buyer.

  • Agent listing: wide exposure, with showings, a lender's appraisal and the chance a buyer's financing falls through.
  • Owner-handled sale: you set price and terms, and your attorney drafts the contract and deed.
  • Cash purchase: no repair requests and no mortgage contingency, since the buyer takes the property in its present state.

All three finish the same way: a notarized deed, transfer tax forms for the Erie County Clerk, and payment of whatever tax is still owed on the parcel.

Lancaster sits in Erie County, roughly 11 miles east of downtown Buffalo, on about 37 square miles. Two villages lie inside it, Lancaster and Depew. Population is 45,075, close to the 45,106 counted in 2020.

Five school districts bill Lancaster addresses: Lancaster Central, Depew Union Free, Alden Central, Clarence Central and Iroquois Central. Most of the town is in Lancaster Central, but the district printed on your tax bill is the one to quote to buyers. The Thruway (I-90) crosses the north end, US 20 follows Broadway through the middle, and NY 78 (Transit Road) forms the western edge, so getting around by car is easy.

Owners near Broadway in the village should ask the village what historic review applies before promising a buyer a facade or window project. The Building Department's page carries a Village of Lancaster historic preservation application.

The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $277,600, and about four in five homes are lived in by their owners. A survey midpoint cannot price an individual house, so ask for recent nearby sales before you settle on a number.

Gross rent is $1,079 at the midpoint and household income $89,080. The town counts 19,722 households, and 22.1% of its residents are 65 or older. A 20-minute average commute is one of the quieter selling points for a house here.

Past work can come up in a sale. The Building Department enforces the state building and fire code, zoning, stormwater practices and flood plain rules across both the town and the village, and nobody may build, alter, move or demolish a structure without a permit.

The office posts applications for decks, fences, pools and hot tubs, sheds, signs, demolition and one- and two-family dwellings, along with a handout on as-built survey requirements. If a deck, an addition or a finished basement went in before you bought, ask whether the project is on file and was signed off. A clear answer saves negotiating time later.

  • Inspections tied to a permit are booked by phone with the office, which keeps weekday hours.
  • The department also links resources on vacant and "zombie" properties, handy for an inherited house that has sat empty.
  • Truck routes and yard sale permits are separate matters handled through the town and its Highway Department.

Town and County bills are due February 15 and school bills October 15, moving a day later if the date lands on a weekend or holiday. The tax office inside the Town Clerk's office collects both. A mailed check counts as on time only when the postmark carries the due date or an earlier one, with no exceptions.

Lancaster late-payment rules
BillLate penaltyWhere unpaid tax goes
School (due October 15)7.5% for the rest of October, 9% through NovemberErie County tax roll after November 30
Town and County (due February 15)1.5% in the first two weeks, rising to 7.5% by end of April, then interestErie County after June 30

The town office takes Town and County payments through June 30 and school payments through November 30. Past those dates, payments and payoff questions go to Erie County Real Property Tax Services in Buffalo. Interest changes the payoff every month, so ask the county for a figure before you fix a closing date.

sections.h2: Erie County deed charges and transfer tax
sections.html:
Erie County adds its own transfer tax to the state's, for a combined $4.50 per $500 of price: $2.00 state and $2.50 county. The seller is responsible for it, and the Clerk rounds the price up to the next $500.

Recording adds a $45 statutory fee, $5 for each page, $10 to file the TP-584 and $125 to file the RP-5217 report for residential property. The deed must carry original signatures, a notary's acknowledgment, a full legal description and street addresses for every party, since P.O. boxes are rejected.

  • An owner aged 62 or older who has lived in a one- or two-family house for a year or more can claim the reduced $2.00-per-$500 rate.
  • Residential sales at $1 million or above add a 1% mansion tax that the buyer pays.
  • The Clerk also asks for a Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership on residential property.

The TP-584 and payment are due 15 days after delivery of the deed. Afterward, close out your STAR registration so the new owner can register for the credit.

sections.h2: Sorting out a damaged or inherited house
sections.html:
A damaged house is still sellable. You can market it as-is to investors, list it and price in the repairs, or take cash from a buyer who needs no repair list. Call the Building Department about open permits before you accept any offer.

With a cash sale there is no appraisal and no loan approval to wait on. The steps are a written offer, a title search, signing the deed and transfer forms, and payment at closing. Gather your latest tax bills, any permit paperwork and, for an estate, the papers showing who may sign. Ask the tax office and the county for payoff figures so the closing attorney can pay any unpaid tax out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: Which office collects tax on a Lancaster property?
faqs.a: The Lancaster tax office, part of the Town Clerk's office, collects Town, County and school bills. Later payments, after June 30 for Town and County or November 30 for school, go to Erie County Real Property Tax Services in Buffalo.

faqs.q: Does Lancaster belong to one school district?
faqs.a: No. Lancaster Central covers most of it, yet Depew Union Free, Alden Central, Clarence Central and Iroquois Central also bill Lancaster addresses. Read your own tax bill to see which one applies.

faqs.q: Who covers transfer tax on a Lancaster sale?
faqs.a: The seller covers the state and Erie County transfer tax when the deed reaches the County Clerk. The total is $4.50 per $500, and qualifying owners aged 62 and over may pay a reduced $2.00 rate.

faqs.q: Must I get a permit before listing my Lancaster house?
faqs.a: A plain sale is not among the permit triggers. The rule covers building, altering, moving and demolishing, so call the Building Department to confirm that earlier decks, pools or additions were permitted and closed out.

faqs.q: Is a damaged Lancaster house still sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. You can market it as-is to investors, list it and price in the repairs, or take cash from a buyer who purchases without a repair list. Check with the Building Department about open permits before accepting any offer.
